lead: Knock, acceleration, torque and angular-rate sensors turn mechanical vibration and motion into electrical signals. The engine ECU uses a knock sensor to hear detonation and retard spark before damage. Airbag and ESP systems use accelerometers and gyroscopes to detect a crash or a skid. Torque sensors measure shaft twist; LIDAR measures distance by light time of flight; flex-fuel sensors measure ethanol content. These sensors protect the engine and stabilise the vehicle, so they sit in both engine control and safety systems.
prereq: You need: sensor basics and signal conditioning; Hall, reluctance and optical sensors; basic mechanics (F = m a, strain).

blocks.text: Knock is the self-ignition of the unburnt end gas ahead of the flame front, after the spark. The sharp pressure waves it sets up ring the engine block at a frequency set by the combustion chamber, usually in the 5–15 kHz band. A piezoelectric knock sensor bolts to the block. Its crystal makes charge when the block vibrates. Charge sensitivity d is often given in pC/N. A charge amplifier converts this charge to a voltage. A band-pass filter then keeps only the knock band. A rectifier and an integrator (a low-pass smoothing stage) turn the burst into one number per firing. The ECU opens a window from the crank-angle signal in the combustion period, roughly 10° to 60° after top dead centre, and compares that number with a threshold learnt from the quiet cylinders. Above threshold, it retards the spark of that cylinder by a few degrees and then creeps it back. The window stops the ECU reacting to valve or injector noise at other crank angles.
q = d F,   V = q / C<sub>f</sub>
blocks.where: q is charge (C); d is charge sensitivity (C/N); F is knock force (N); V is output voltage (V); C<sub>f</sub> is feedback capacitance (F).

blocks.text: A MEMS accelerometer has a proof mass on silicon springs. Comb fingers on the mass form capacitors with fixed fingers. Acceleration moves the mass, so one capacitance rises and the other falls. The circuit reads the differential capacitance, which is proportional to acceleration. A high-g accelerometer in the airbag system detects a crash pulse. A low-g lateral accelerometer in ESP measures cornering. Some syllabi call the lateral accelerometer and yaw-rate gyro the ESP sensors. A MEMS gyroscope vibrates a proof mass and uses the Coriolis force to measure angular rate. The output is rate in °/s, not angle. The ECU can integrate rate to get angle, but bias and noise make the angle drift. Vehicle stability algorithms combine rate, lateral acceleration, wheel speeds and steering angle. The control law belongs to the electronic stability program in vehicle motion control.

Torque sensors measure twist in a shaft. A strain-gauge bridge bonded to the shaft changes resistance with shear strain. A magnetoelastic shaft changes magnetic permeability when twisted; a coil reads the change. A surface-acoustic-wave (SAW) torque sensor uses a wave delay that changes with strain. These sensors help transmission control and electric power steering. A strain-gauge torque sensor on a steering column helps electric power steering apply assist in proportion to driver torque. LIDAR measures distance by time of flight. A light pulse leaves the sensor, reflects from an object and returns. The round-trip distance is c t, so d = c t / 2. Here d is distance (m), c is speed of light (3×10⁸ m/s), and t is round-trip time (s). A flex-fuel sensor estimates ethanol in petrol. Ethanol has a higher dielectric constant than petrol, so a capacitive sensor changes with fuel composition. The ECU then adjusts fuel quantity and spark timing. How driver assistance uses LIDAR belongs to vehicle motion control and safety.

spec.aria: Five blocks: piezo sensor, 2 picocoulombs per newton times 50 newtons gives 100 picocoulombs; charge amplifier with 1000 picofarads gives 0.10 volts; band-pass 5 to 15 kilohertz; rectify and integrate; compare in window and retard spark. Below, a crank-angle axis with the spark before TDC and a knock window from 10 to 60 degrees after, holding a decaying burst.

examples.question: A piezoelectric knock sensor has charge sensitivity d = 2 pC/N. A knock force of 50 N acts on it. The charge amplifier has feedback capacitor C<sub>f</sub> = 1000 pF. Find the charge produced and the output voltage.
examples.answer: The charge is 100 pC and the charge-amplifier output is 0.10 V.
examples.check:
d = 2e-12
F = 50.0
q = d * F
Cf = 1000e-12
V = q / Cf
print(q * 1e12)
print(V)

examples.question: A car at 50 km/h hits a barrier and the passenger cell stops in 80 ms. (a) Find the average deceleration in m/s² and in g. (b) A MEMS accelerometer has a proof mass of 2 µg (2 × 10⁻⁹ kg) on springs of total stiffness 2 N/m, with comb gaps of 2 µm. Find the proof-mass movement and the fractional change in one gap.
steps: Average deceleration: a = Δv ÷ Δt = 13.89 ÷ 0.080 = 173.6 m/s², that is 173.6 ÷ 9.81 = 17.7 g.
Spring force balances the inertia force: k x = m a, so x = m a ÷ k = 2 × 10⁻⁹ × 173.6 ÷ 2 = 1.74 × 10⁻⁷ m = 0.174 µm.
Fractional gap change: x ÷ d = 0.174 ÷ 2 = 0.087, so one gap shrinks by 8.7 % and the opposite one grows by 8.7 %.
Since C = ε₀A ÷ d, one capacitance rises and the other falls by about 9 %; the circuit reads that difference.
Check: the peaks of a real crash pulse are two to three times the average, which is why airbag sensors are specified for ±50 g or more.
examples.answer: Average deceleration 173.6 m/s² (17.7 g); the proof mass moves 0.174 µm, changing each comb gap by 8.7 %.

traps: Do not amplify all engine noise: knock detection uses a band-pass filter around the knock frequency and a crank-angle window.
A gyroscope measures angular rate, not angle; integrating rate drifts because of bias and noise.
Piezo charge sensitivity is in pC/N (or pC/g), and the charge-amplifier output is q ÷ C<sub>f</sub>; using the cable capacitance in place of C<sub>f</sub> gives the wrong voltage.
LIDAR time of flight is round trip: divide c t by 2. Mixing ns and s gives a factor of 10⁹ error.
A torque sensor measures shaft torque, not engine brake torque; mounting and shaft material affect sensitivity.

quiz.q: What physical quantity does a knock sensor measure, and what does the ECU do with it?
quiz.a: It measures structure-borne vibration in the engine block in the knock band. The ECU retards spark angle to stop detonation.

quiz.q: Why is a band-pass filter used in the knock channel instead of a wideband amplifier?
quiz.a: Engine noise covers many frequencies. The 5–15 kHz band contains knock energy and rejects valve and injector noise. A crank-angle window further limits listening to the firing event.

quiz.q: A piezo knock sensor has d = 5 pC/N. A knock force is 40 N. Feedback capacitor C<sub>f</sub> = 2000 pF. Find charge and output voltage.
A yaw-rate gyro outputs 30 °/s for 2 s. The ECU integrates it and gets 60°, but the true angle is 55°. Give two reasons and one fix.
quiz.a: Bias offset and noise integrate into drift; temperature changes bias. Fix: zero the gyro when the vehicle is stationary and fuse with steering angle or accelerometer.

quiz.q: What does a MEMS capacitive accelerometer use as its moving part?
quiz.a: A proof mass with comb fingers that changes differential capacitance when accelerated.

quiz.q: Why does a piezoelectric knock sensor need a charge amplifier rather than a simple voltage amplifier?
quiz.a: The piezo source has very high output impedance and cable capacitance shunts charge. A charge amplifier holds the input near virtual ground and sets gain by C<sub>f</sub>, so cable capacitance has little effect.

quiz.q: A LIDAR pulse returns after 200 ns. Take c = 3×10⁸ m/s. Find the distance.
quiz.a: Round trip: 2d = c t = 3×10⁸ × 200×10⁻⁹ = 60 m. d = 30 m.

beyond: Not for the exam. Automotive MEMS now combine a 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyro in one inertial measurement unit for ESP and ADAS. Piezoelectric MEMS and thin-film sensors are replacing some bulk ceramics. Magnetoelastic and SAW torque sensors are used in electric power steering and driveline test benches. Researchers are working on optical and chip-scale LIDAR for ADAS. Search terms: MEMS comb accelerometer, Coriolis vibratory gyroscope, magnetoelastic torque sensor, SAW torque sensor, flex-fuel dielectric sensor, automotive LiDAR time of flight.
